Evidence boundary

A Zenodo deposit is a citable public record; it does not by itself imply peer review, independent validation, or broader empirical generalization.

01 / record overview

What this record documents.

This Zenodo software release packages the Level-1 computational stack used across several VARZIN lines of work. The deposited overview identifies a finite-affine core, genomic scanning utilities, a torus-manifold numerical solver, and additional auditing code. Its role in the research record is primarily reproducibility: it provides concrete implementation artifacts that can be inspected independently of broader interpretive claims attached to the project.

Research question

Can the computational components underlying the Level-1 VARZIN architecture be preserved as inspectable, citable software artifacts whose behavior can be evaluated separately from speculative interpretation?

This question is interpreted within the documented model, dataset, implementation, and evaluation procedure; it is not generalized beyond that evidence.

04 / contribution

What this record adds to the research trail.

The release makes the implementation layer explicit. Mathematical, numerical, genomic, and auditing components can be examined as software without treating the existence of code as validation of any physical, biological, cognitive, or semantic hypothesis.

Version v2.0.0 is the listed software release. Results should be attributed to the documented code, dependencies, inputs, and assumptions rather than generalized beyond the implementation.
